note: Draft vectors for LIP-0026 sections 9 and 10, the landlord class and rows without a certifier (J10, with the co-author's agreement pending, and J9, decided and agreed by both owners on 2026-11-15, whose vectors rest on the checks of J10 and the holders of J11). The scripts of the recipient name and of the inputs of the operation that created its current output are octets, and so are the name values; the history of a landlord is stated, as in the walks of the LIP-0021 vectors. No vector reads a chain, and no signature in this file verifies: the octets of signatures are placeholders. Every output of this file is taken as confirmed at or above the height from which the chain enforces the witness rules, so that the reading of a witness key hash does not depend on a height (LIP-0021 O3.3). Keys are multiples of the generator of secp256k1 and belong to nobody. A refused admission holds one finding and names a passing neighbour that differs from it in that finding; one marked compound holds two and names none. The transfer and return of class-14 is one event with two facts: an output of the stretch reads as another key, and that key wrote the current value. The eight codes that begin with CLASS are proposals. Two admissions end with a code of LIP-0021, listed in codes_of_lip_0021: the proof of the recipient by name stands before the checks of a class (R9.9), and that code keeps its meaning. No verdict of this file records a closure.

fields.templates: issuer is what the parent binds for its issuer; notaries are the names of the notaries that it pins; recipient has exactly one of request_public_key, name with owner_public_key, or class; certifier is a name or null.
fields.admissions: row is the template of the child's row. context states the heights of the parent's recent block and of the tip. node.recipient_name gives the script of the current output of the recipient name and the inputs of the operation that created it: for each input the script of the output that it spends, its unlocking script and, where it has one, the items of its witness. node.landlords gives, for a landlord name, its pinned registration, its history from the current output back, its current value and whether a pending transaction spends its current output. An output of a history states its height, its prefix, the reading of its script against the pinned owner key and the outcome of the writer check for the operation that created it; the fifth step of check (b) reads that of the current output. The writer of an update follows from the output before it, which its name input spends: written by the owner or unsupported after an output of the pinned owner, written by another after an output of another key, unsupported after an unsupported one. child.recipient states the name and the owner key that the child signs; the proof of LIP-0021 section 7.2 reads the current output against that key. expect.attestation says whether the checks of the attestation follow (required) or the attestation is not read.

rules.title: the three forms of a recipient constraint, and a class
a child of a class row names its recipient by name
check (a): an agent of a listed landlord
check (b): the six steps on the landlord
check (c): a holder holds the name
check (d): a holder wrote the value
one observation, and the request key
rules.not_covered: No vector holds an observation or a request.

rules.title: the signer of a holder key
the signer of the issuer
rules.not_covered: A rule for the signer of the issuer; a verifier does not see it.

rules.title: what a row without a certifier may name
an exact name is checked against the issuer
no stop coin
rules.not_covered: No vector of this file holds a stop coin.

templates.claim: A class of one landlord and a certifier that the parent pins.
A class of two landlords and a certifier.
No certifier, and a class of exactly the issuer's landlord. The parent pins no notary.
No certifier, and an exact name with its owner key.
No certifier in this template, in a parent that pins a notary: another template of the parent may name it.
A request key and a certifier.
A class that states one name twice, with two registrations.
A constraint that states a request key and a class.
S9-3. No certifier, and a request key.
S9-4. No certifier, and a class of the issuer's landlord and a second one.
S9-4. No certifier, and a class of one landlord that is not the issuer.
No certifier, and a class of the issuer's name with another registration than the parent binds.
No certifier, and a class of the issuer's name and registration with another owner key.
A certifier that the parent does not pin.

admissions.claim: The control. The recipient name is an agent of the landlord, the holder h1 holds it, and the update that wrote its value spent the previous output of the name, which h1 held. The landlord's history is unbroken from its registration.
The holder h2 wrote the value and sent the name to the holder h1. Two holders, both listed.
A holder registered the name: the name input of the registration spends the reservation that the holder made.
The previous output of the name was a witness key hash of the holder, and the update spends it with a witness.
A class of two landlords. The recipient points to the second, whose holder h3 holds the name and wrote its value. The first landlord is not read.
A child of a class row that names a request key.
The value of the recipient name is a landlord binding and no agent binding.
The value points to a landlord that the class does not list.
The value points to a name that differs from the listed one in the case of one letter.
The value has no swarma member.
The landlord's current output is 36000 blocks below the tip: the name is expired.
The walk of the landlord ends at another registration than the pinned one.
The pinned registration is confirmed above the recent block of the parent.

A transfer and a return: between the recent block and the tip one output of the landlord reads as another key, and the current one is the pinned owner's again. The other key signed the return, so it also wrote the current value; the fourth step reports before the fifth.
The same change of owner below the recent block: it is outside the stretch, and the class admits. The pinned owner wrote the current value after the return.

The landlord's name came to the pinned owner by a transfer below the recent block, and the owner has written no value since. The operation that created the current output spent an output of another key: the pinned owner did not write the value that carries the holders.
The reading node holds a pending transaction that spends the landlord's current output.
The node keeps no transaction index: the walk of the landlord proves nothing.
An output of the landlord's stretch has a script that the profile does not support.
The landlord's value has no holders.
The landlord's value has an empty list.
The key that holds the recipient name is not in the landlord's list.
The landlord removed the holder h1 from its list: the names that h1 holds refuse from that value on.
The landlord's list has its two pins in descending order: the value refuses under LIP-0010 section 10, and the landlord has no readable list.

The gift. An attacker held the name, wrote a value that points to the landlord with a channel key of its own, and sent the output to the address of the holder h1. Checks (a), (b) and (c) pass. The name input of that update spent an output of the attacker.
The gift by a registration: the attacker made the reservation and registered the name straight to the holder's address.

The gifted name of class-25 after the holder h1 made an update of its own that repeats the value. The check looks at that one operation and passes: R9.11 is the rule against it, and no verifier sees its breach.
The holder's signature on the name input has the hash type 03 and not 01: the writer check is unsupported.
The current output of the recipient name has a script without a supported address. The proof of the recipient by name refuses it (LIP-0021 O7.2, row 3), and no check of the class is reached.
Two findings: the value points to an unlisted landlord, and an attacker wrote it. Check (a) reports.
Two findings: a pending operation of the landlord, and a holder that the list does not name. Check (b) reports.
Two findings: the key that holds the name is not listed, and it is also the key that wrote the value. Check (c) reports.
Two findings inside check (b): the landlord's value was written by another key, and a pending transaction spends its current output. The fifth step reports.

The child signs the owner key of the holder h2, and the holder h1 holds the name and wrote its value. Every check of the class would pass. The proof of the recipient by name refuses first (LIP-0021 O7.2, row 2).
A class of two landlords. The recipient points to the first, whose holder h1 holds the name and wrote its value. The control of class-36 and class-37.

The gift by a holder of a co-listed landlord. The class lists two landlords. The holder h3 of the second wrote a value that points to the first and sent the name to the holder h1 of the first. The writer is a holder of a landlord of the class, and not of the landlord that the value names.

The holder h3 of the second landlord holds a name whose value points to the first, and a holder of the first wrote that value. The key that holds the name is a holder of a landlord of the class, and not of the landlord that the value names.

The mirror of class-36: the landlord that the value names is the second of the class. The holder h1 of the first landlord wrote a value that points to the second and sent the name to the holder h3 of the second. It differs from class-05 in the name input alone, which spends an output of h1 and is signed by h1 with the hash type 01.

The mirror of class-37: the value points to the second landlord, and its holder h3 wrote it. The holder h1 of the first landlord holds the name, and the child signs the owner key of h1. It differs from class-05 in the key that holds the name.
S9-1. A row without a certifier whose class is the issuer's landlord. The child needs no attestation.
S9-2. The same child, presented with an attestation. The attestation is not read.
A row without a certifier whose recipient is an exact name. The name is an agent of the issuer's landlord, a holder holds it and wrote its value.
S9-5. The exact name of such a row points to another landlord than the issuer.
S9-6. The exact name points to the issuer's landlord and a holder holds it, and an attacker wrote its value.
The exact name is held by a key that the issuer's landlord does not list.
A pending transaction spends the current output of the issuer's name.
The same exact name in a row with a certifier. The checks of a class are not made, and the child is certified as before: the name need not be an agent of the issuer.
S9-K1, a known limit. The recipient of the parent belongs to another owner; nothing in the row or in the child says so, and the child of certifier-01 is admitted.

The exact name of a row without a certifier, and the issuer's name came to its owner by a transfer below the recent block: another key wrote the value that carries the holders. The fifth step of check (b) is made for an exact name as well.
The same history of the issuer's name under a row without a certifier whose class is the issuer's landlord. The two forms of such a row decide alike.
